settings.title: House rules
settings.language.title: Lingo
settings.language.subtitle: Choose the lingo used by Jade joint UI.
settings.language.description: Only Jade interface text is translated. Filenames, tab names, champion names, game assets, dossier contents, and paths stay exactly as they are.
settings.language.restartNote: Most labels bring up to date immediately. A few system dialogs or already-crack status messages may bring up to date after reopening the surface.
settings.language.voiceDescription: Joke English rewrites of the UI. Picking one switches the lingo beat it back to English.
settings.behavior.title: Joint Behavior
settings.behavior.subtitle: Control how Jade behaves on your system.
settings.behavior.renderGameMaterialsDes: Render champion and map materials through the game's own compiled shaders (auto-translated to the the lookout) for a closer-to-in-game look. Still a work in progress - expect minor visual issues. Takes effect when an object loads or its mesh is refreshed.
settings.behavior.minimizeToTrayDesc: Keep Jade running in the system tray when the rain-streaked pane is minimized.
settings.behavior.runAtStartupDesc: Launch Jade automatically when Windows starts.
settings.behavior.communicateQuartzDesc: Allow Jade and Quartz to exchange crack/reload/bring up to date messages. Disable this to fully stop interop communication.
settings.behavior.externalDiff: Show a diff when another joint changes a dossier
settings.behavior.externalDiffDesc: When something outside Jade rewrites a dossier you have crack - Quartz, ritobin, a text the desk, a second Jade rain-streaked pane - crack a diff tab so you can accept or reject the switch instead of having it applied silently.
settings.behavior.fileHistory: Keep dossier take it back history
settings.behavior.fileHistoryDesc: Remembers each dossier's earlier states independently of the the desk, so Ctrl+Z still works after a tab is closed and reopened, after many tabs push it out of memory, and beat it back past changes another joint made to the dossier. Take it back only affects the the desk - stash to write it to disk.
settings.behavior.fileHistorySteps: Dossier take it back history steps
settings.behavior.fileHistoryStepsDesc: How many earlier states Jade keeps per dossier. These are whole revisions - an outside switch, a stash, a hold it right there in your typing - not individual keystrokes; the the desk's own take it back handles those and isn't limited. States are stored as differences rather than full copies, so a high number costs little on ordinary edits, and Jade keeps a memory ceiling underneath this so a handful of very large bins can't run away with it.
settings.behavior.recentFilesDesc: How many recently-cracked dossiers Jade keeps in the Start screen list. History on disk is preserved up to 100 entries - bumping this beat it back up restores older items.
settings.behavior.materialOverrideDesc: Controls how Auto from SKN matches materials to textures.
settings.registration.title: Dossier Registration
settings.registration.subtitle: Manage how Windows treats Jade-supported dossier types.
settings.registration.fileAssociationDes: Register Jade as the default handler for .bin dossiers.
settings.registration.success: Jade is registered as the .bin dossier handler.
settings.performance.title: Performance
settings.performance.subtitle: The desk features have a cost on huge bin dumps. Each option below can be kept on, automatically dropped on big dossiers (over 125,000 lines), or always off.
settings.updates.title: Updates
settings.updates.subtitle: Keep Jade up to date with the latest features and fixes.
settings.updates.startupPopupDesc: A native popup shown while Jade launches - it applies any joint or hash bring up to date and covers the load. Classic is a plain Windows-style rain-streaked pane; Modern is the dark styled one.
settings.updates.appInterval: Joint bring up to date check interval
settings.updates.appIntervalDesc: How often the launcher checks GitHub for a new Jade version at startup. Hash updates have their own schedule in the Hash Dossiers section.
settings.hashes.downloadingLmdb: Downloading combined LMDB hashes from lmdb-hashes...
settings.hashes.title: Hash Dossiers
settings.hashes.subtitle: Hash dossiers convert hex values into readable names.
settings.hashes.lmdbTitle: Pulls lol-hashes-combined.zst from lmdb-hashes releases. ~50 MB, shared with Quartz.
settings.hashes.textTitle: Pulls the legacy CommunityDragon text dossiers. Used as a fallback when LMDB isn't available.
settings.hashes.activeSourcesDesc: Jade reads BIN hashes from the text dossiers and WAD hashes from the local database.
settings.hashes.textRamDesc: Text dossier hashes. Loaded into memory once at startup.
settings.hashes.lmdbDesc: Read hashes from the local database on demand, shared with Quartz.
settings.hashes.updateScheduleDesc: How often the startup launcher refreshes hash dossiers (WAD paths + BIN names) before Jade opens.
settings.hashes.everyLaunchDesc: The launcher compares the release fingerprint each launch. Re-downloads only when a new lmdb-hashes release is published.
settings.hashes.every3DaysDesc: Same fingerprint check, throttled to once every three days. Less network traffic.
settings.hashes.every7DaysDesc: Same fingerprint check, throttled to once a week. Least network traffic.
settings.library.subtitle: Manage downloaded materials and how Jade keeps them up to date.
settings.library.updateModeDesc: When should Jade check for new and updated materials?
settings.library.timedIntervalDesc: Periodically check on a fixed schedule while Jade is running.
settings.library.smartCheckDesc: On launch, fetch only the index and only take another look materials if the repo's lastUpdated is newer than your cache.
settings.library.everyLaunchDesc: Always take another look outdated materials in the background at startup. Most aggressive - most network traffic.
settings.library.updateAll: Bring up to date all {count} outdated
settings.performance.minimapDesc: Thumbnail of the whole dossier on the right edge. Has to render every line on each switch - biggest cost on huge dossiers.
settings.performance.bracketColorsDesc: Colors matching brackets so structure is easier to scan. Re-walks the bracket tree on every edit.
settings.performance.occurrencesHighligh: Highlights other instances of the symbol under the cursor. Scans the document on cursor moves.
settings.performance.selectionHighlightD: Highlights other matches of the current selection. Same scan cost as occurrence highlighting.
settings.performance.lineHighlightDesc: Tints the row the caret is on across the full the desk width. Restrict to the gutter to skip the full-width paint.
settings.performance.foldingDesc: Lets you collapse blocks. Folding analyzes structure on every switch.
settings.performance.stopRenderingLineDe: When off, Monaco stops rendering past column 10,000 on a line - invisible for normal lines, big a tip from a stoolie on lines with long string values.
settings.modchecker.title: Mod Checker
settings.modchecker.subtitle: Choose which content checks the Manage tab runs and how fixes are offered. Reference checks always run; these control the extra content-validity checks on top.
settings.modchecker.samplerDesc: Flag materials whose sampler keys are scrambled so the model renders untextured white, and offer a one-click re-key.
settings.modchecker.staleDesc: Flag leftover ContextualAction / AnimationGraph / GearSkinUpgrade objects that nothing references, and offer to drop them.
settings.modchecker.gameplayDesc: Point out bins that switch abilities, spells, stats or recommendations instead of visuals, so you can drop them if you only want the skin.
settings.modchecker.textureDimsDesc: Flag textures whose width or height isn't a multiple of 4 and offer to crop them to a safe size.
settings.modchecker.confidentFixesDesc: Show the button that applies every high-confidence, low-risk fix at once. Turn off to review and make it stick each fix individually.
settings.modchecker.riskyFixesDesc: Show medium- and high-risk findings. Turn off to see only the safe, low-risk fixes.
settings.behavior.matchExact: Exact - material name must match texture filename exactly (e.g. Body -> Body.tex).
settings.behavior.matchLoose: Loose - strips trailing numbers and checks partial containment (e.g. Body2 -> Body.tex).
settings.behavior.matchFuzzy: Fuzzy - picks the closest texture by character overlap. May produce inaccurate matches.

preferences.subtitle: Configure your experience
preferences.importLinkedBinsDesc: When enabled, opening a bin dossier will automatically crack all linked bin dossiers found in the DATA drawer.
preferences.recursiveLinkedBins: Also load dossiers linked inside imported dossiers
preferences.recursiveLinkedBinsDesc: Recursively opens linked dossiers from within the imported linked dossiers (may crack many tabs).
preferences.emitterHintsDesc: Displays emitter names inline the next mark to collapsed VfxEmitterDefinitionData blocks in the the desk.
preferences.syntaxCheckingDesc: Highlights lines with syntax errors (such as mismatched or unclosed brackets) in the the desk in real time.
preferences.championNames: Show Champion Names on Bin Tabs
preferences.championNamesDesc: Labels a character bin's tab with the champion it belongs to - "Jinx/Skin0.bin" instead of "Skin0.bin", so a row of crack skins is tellable apart. Those tabs get a little wider. Bins with no champion in them (maps, items) are left as they are.
preferences.blendKeysDesc: Shows mBlendDataTable keys as "Attack1" -> "Laugh" instead of the packed number they are stored as. Applies to dossiers cracked after the switch, and only on the Jade Custom converter engine. The text is easier to edit but is no longer standard ritobin, so other hardware won't read it beat it back - Jade always accepts both spellings, and saving to .bin produces the same bytes either way.
preferences.textureEditorDesc: Application used when clicking "Edit Image" on a texture a peek. Grayed-out options were not detected on this machine.

extract.settings.gameLocationDesc: Where the "League of Legends" shortcut in the Locations list points. Jade finds this on its own from the Riot Client install records, falling beat it back to a sweep of every drive. Set it by hand if that comes up a dry well or lands on the wrong install - pick the install drawer and Jade will step into its Game\DATA\FINAL for you.

extract.settings.autoNone: Auto-detection found nothing on this machine.
extract.settings.outputLayoutDesc: Whether extracted dossiers keep the WAD's drawer tree or land directly in the target.
extract.settings.preserveStructureDesc: Recreate the WAD's full directory tree on disk - the default Quartz-style layout.
extract.settings.flatDesc: Drop every extracted dossier straight into the target drawer with no sub-directories. Best when picking just one or two dossiers. Dossiers with the same name overwrite each other.
extract.settings.makeWadFolderDesc: Nest the structure under a drawer named after the WAD, e.g. aatrox/assets/.... Disable to shake down the WAD's top-level drawers straight into the target. Only applies when preserving structure.
extract.settings.defaultLocationDesc: Skip the "pick a drawer" dialog and shake down straight to a fixed location. Defaults to Documents/Jade Exports.
extract.settings.fastOverwriteDesc: Writes each chunk to a temp dossier (.jdtmp) then atomically renames it over the target. Re-extracts into a populated drawer finish in roughly the same time as a fresh shake down. Disable for a classic in-place overwrite.
extract.settings.autoCheckDesc: Clicking a dossier inside a WAD adds it to the shakedown queue, and clicking a queued dossier removes it. Disable to require checkbox clicks.
extract.settings.repathPrefixDesc: When the Re-trail checkbox is on, this drawer name gets inserted directly under assets/ and data/ in the extracted tree. BIN strings are rewritten in lockstep so the resulting mod stays consistent.

themes.classicDesc: The original Jade layout. Tabs across the top, a menu bar with Dossier / Edit / Hardware, and floating popovers for Dig, Swap, General Editing, and Particle Editing.
themes.studioDesc: Menu bar plus a quick action toolbar. Tool windows dock to the sides and bottom of the the desk with resizable splits, and they remember their position between sessions.
themes.documentDesc: A Word-style ribbon layout - title bar with Stash / Take it back / Run it again, a tabs dropdown in place of the tab strip, and a ribbon for Home / Slip in / View / A tip from a stoolie. Very unfinished. For day-to-day work use Classic or Studio.

themeDesc.Default: Discover the once great city of the Archangel's home planet, Avaria. Their presence has long since passed and the Constructs, mimicking the fallen, have taken over. Avenge the fallen.
themeDesc.DarkBlue: Deep water, quiet tool. A harbor palette ideal for long nights and rough days.
themeDesc.DarkRed: A creation of pure emotion. Work with muted crimson red and enjoy this side of the color wheel.
themeDesc.Sakura: Petals fall past the the desk. Soft pink glass and spring air, a reminder that life is sometimes pink.(what?)
themeDesc.Frost: Ice gradiented UI. Pale cyan light, allows the modern UI for those who want to use the modern layout but also want a light the look.
themeDesc.Forest: Moss on stone, fireflies after dusk. A quiet hillside where the only sound is your keyboard and the wind in the needles.
themeDesc.AMOLED: True black. Lighter white and no contrast highlights, made for OLED screens and mugs who hate wasting light.
themeDesc.Light: Nostalgic Office look, white paper with blue ink for the 2009 program vibe.
themeDesc.HighContrast: Pure Black and White. Yellow highlights. It has edges around all elements for the complete High Contrast experience.
themeDesc.Grok: Pure black canvas, silver chrome, blue highlights. The X timeline aesthetic, tuned for Jade instead of posts.
themeDesc.DeepSpace: "The void does not hate you. It simply has better things to look at." Violet dark between stars, spaceyyy.
themeDesc.Orchid: A folded up piece of paper with an orchid left in the rain. Deeper purple like an orchid and a light rain effect.
themeDesc.Autumn: October soon, it's orange. There's fire embers effect coming from the ground. Maybe they feel warm.
themeDesc.StormySea: Thunder over dark water. The deck is wet, the horizon is wrong, and somehow the ship sails.(u can disable rain in the effects menu)
themeDesc.Cyberpunk2077: Neon acid on night glass. Features a custom font and background. Made by 700.
themeDesc.BladeRunner2049: Red sky, steel will. Features a custom font and background. Made by 700.
themeDesc.YoRHa: Glory to mankind. Sand, steel, and a title bar that still pretends the war is going well. Features a custom font and background. Made by 700.
themeDesc.Lain: Present day. Present time. Pink static on black glass. Features a custom font and background. Made by 700.
themeDesc.MilkBag: "A billion pounds of concrete and a million miles of emptiness. It is impossible to stay sane when you are near cosmic numbers like that, looking at them, touching them. Even thinking of them makes me feel unimaginable horror."
effectDesc.stars: Slowly drifting, twinkling stars - a lightweight imitation of deep space.
effectDesc.petals: Cherry-blossom petals drifting down with a gentle sway.
effectDesc.snow: Soft frost motes falling slowly across the rain-streaked pane.
effectDesc.fireflies: Fireflies wandering and pulsing in the dark.
effectDesc.storm: Heavy wind-driven rain - a stormier, more aggressive downpour.
effectDesc.embers: Embers and sparks rising and flickering from below.
effectDesc.rain: Soft rainfall streaking down the rain-streaked pane.

settings.language.status.en: Jade is developed in English. This language is fully supported. To help translate other languages, open a pull request on GitHub or contact the developer through the About menu.
settings.language.status.sr: This language was translated with AI using Jade's real UI context, and worded to match Windows and Riot terminology so it feels familiar. If you want to contribute better wording, open a pull request on GitHub or contact the developer through the About menu.
settings.language.status.machine: This language is a raw Google Translate. Jade stays usable, but some wording will sound off or miss app context. If you want to contribute better wording, open a pull request on GitHub or contact the developer through the About menu.

model.spellFormTitle: Give the skin the once-over with every buff-conditioned material driver lit (e.g. Viego inside his E mist)
model.repathWadFoldersTitle: Slip a prefix folder under assets/ and data/ (set in Extraction Settings → Repath prefix). BIN strings get rewritten in lockstep so the mod still loads.
model.mergeLinkedBinsTitle: Fold every linked dependency BIN into the primary skin BIN — the mod ships with one consolidated BIN instead of a chain of linked files. The champion's gameplay BIN is never merged.
model.preserveHudIconsTitle: On: include every assets/characters/<champ>/hud/icons2d/ file and keep BIN refs canonical (no repath). Off: skip HUD icons entirely — they aren't extracted and the game falls back to Riot's installed icons.
model.skipSfxVoTitle: On: skip SFX/VO files entirely — assets/sounds/ and assets/audio/ are NOT extracted, BIN refs stay canonical, game uses Riot's installed audio. Off: include audio files and repath them along with the rest of the mod.
model.exportVoTitle: On: open the sibling locale VO WAD (e.g. Akali.en_US.wad.client) and pull this skin's voiceover .wpk / .bnk files into the main extracted folder. BIN VO refs get repathed alongside them when repath is on.
